definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra acting on V
definitions.definition: U_Z is the integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(C) generated by X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for all integers r≥0; its action on V is the given representation extended to the enveloping algebra.

definitions.type: subring of Q, embedded in C
definitions.definition: R=Z_(p)={a/b∈Q:a,b∈Z and p does not divide b}, with operations inherited from Q. A unit of R means an element having a multiplicative inverse in R.
M_R is the R-span of M in V, namely all finite sums of r_j m_j with r_j∈R and m_j∈M. The canonical map R⊗_Z M→M_R sends r⊗m to rm; its injectivity is to be proved, not assumed.

definitions.type: family of R-submodules of C indexed by I
definitions.definition: For each i∈I, J_i={c∈C:c e_i∈M_R}, with addition and R-action inherited from C.

V(K)=M⊗_Z K. Here tensor products have their usual balanced-module meaning: they are generated by pure tensors subject to additivity in each argument and (am)⊗c=m⊗(ac) for the base scalar a. Induced lattice endomorphisms act on the M factor; the same symbols x,y,h denote these induced K-linear operators once preservation of M is established.
L(K)=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K with the bracket induced by commutators and the action induced from the lattice operators. This is the Chevalley construction, including in characteristic 2.

inputs.statement: p is prime, K has characteristic p, and 0≤λ<p.
V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ and complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generator endomorphisms satisfy hx-xh=2x, hy-yh=-2y, and xy-yx=h.

M is an admissible lattice: it is a free abelian subgroup of V admitting an integer basis that is also a complex basis of V, and is stable under U_Z. The choice of M is arbitrary, not restricted to the minimal lattice.

The integer map Z→K extends to a ring map R→K by a/d↦(a in K)/(d in K). There are natural K-linear isomorphisms M⊗_Z K≃M_R⊗_R K≃(M_R/pM_R)⊗_{F_p}K, where F_p=Z/pZ and its map to K is induced by the integer map. There exists a K-basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} of V(K), arising as the scalar extensions of b e_i for a nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, on which xβ_0=0, xβ_i=(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for i≥1, yβ_i=(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=(λ-2i)β_i, with integer coefficients read in K. For every such basis define ε_ij by ε_ij β_k=δ_jk β_i. All binom(λ,j) and all r! for 0≤r≤λ are nonzero in K; induced divided powers satisfy X_r=(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=(r!)^{-1}y^r in that range, and ε_ij=binom(λ,j)^{-1} X_{λ-i}(Y_λX_λ)Y_{λ-j}. Thus every K-subspace invariant under x,y is invariant under every ε_ij.

output.statement: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W of V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h then W={0} or W=V(K). Equivalently V(K) is a nonzero irreducible L(K)-module.

locals.type: K-basis of V(K) indexed by I
locals.declaration: Choose the K-basis β with matrix-unit identities supplied by N004.
Define ε_ij to be the matrix units of the chosen basis β as in N004.
Fix an arbitrary K-linear subspace W of V(K).
In the nonzero branch choose w≠0 in W using F001 under L2.
Let c be the unique coordinate family of w in the basis β.
Choose j with c_j≠0; equivalently choose the index of a nonzero coordinate of w whose existence is in F001.

argument.text: Choose β and define ε as in N004; H001 gives n=λ+1>0, so I is nonempty. The basis vector β_0 is nonzero, proving V(K)≠0. Fix an arbitrary subspace W and assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. N004 then makes W invariant under every ε_ij. If W={0}, the desired alternative is already true. In the other branch assume L2: W≠{0}. By this assumption W has a nonzero vector; since β is a basis, such a vector has a nonzero coordinate. Record F001 to choose both a vector and an index in the next paragraph.

produces.statement: There exist a nonzero vector z∈W and an index t∈I such that the t-th coordinate of z in β is nonzero. Also W is invariant under every ε_{ii,jj} for ii,jj∈I.

argument.text: Choose the vector w and index j jointly from F001 and let w=∑_{i∈I}c_i β_i be its basis expansion, so c_j≠0. For every i∈I, the matrix-unit formula gives ε_ij w=c_j β_i∈W. Since K is a field, multiplication by c_j^{-1} gives β_i∈W. Every vector of V(K) is a K-linear combination of these basis vectors, so W=V(K). Thus in the nonzero branch the required alternative holds; discharge L2 and combine with the zero branch to get W={0} or W=V(K) under L1.

Discharge L1 and universally quantify the arbitrary W. Together with nonzeroness proved in S001 this proves the asserted subspace statement. For the Lie-algebra formulation, H004 and H002 give lattice preservation of x,y and h=xy-yx, so L(K) acts as defined; invariance under its generator span is equivalent, by linearity, to invariance under x,y,h. Hence the same statement is irreducibility as an L(K)-module. No algebraic closure of K was used. When λ=0, n=1 and all factorials and binomials in the route are 1; the proof remains valid. When p=2, H001 permits λ=0 or 1 and all factorials used have r<2. No distinctness of reduced h-eigenvalues was invoked.
